first_weeks.risk: Around now, weeks often get fuller. One session this week keeps the thread going, whatever shape it takes.

week2.title: Week 2: your first comparison
week2.body: Same move as last week, side by side. This is the honest evidence early on: what you lift.

week3.title: Week 3: how steady you've been
week3.body: How many days you logged, and why we show it: steady logging is what lets the numbers mean something.

week4.title: Week 4: what's changing
week4.body: Most of your strength gain so far is your nervous system learning the moves, not muscle yet. That's normal, and it's the foundation.

week5.title: Week 5: the stretch that counts
week5.body: In gym data, people who reach about nine sessions in six weeks tend to keep going. Each one this week counts toward it.

week6.title: Week 6: six weeks in
week6.body: From here, muscle may start to show in the measurements. Time for your first photo or tape check, if you'd like.

week7.title: Week 7: you, then and now
week7.body: Week 1 next to week 7: your lifts, your consistency, your trend.

week8.title: Week 8: your eight weeks
week8.body: What changed, what didn't, and why. Eight weeks start a habit; the next block makes it yours.

no_training.risk: Around now, weeks often get fuller. Logging a meal or a weigh-in today keeps the thread going, whatever shape the week takes.

week2.title: Week 2: your first comparison
week2.body: This week next to last: what you logged, and where your trend began. Early on, the habit counts more than the number.

week3.title: Week 3: how steady you've been
week3.body: How many days you logged, and why we show it: steady logging is what lets the numbers mean something.

week4.title: Week 4: what's changing
week4.body: Your weight goes up and down day to day; the trend over weeks is what counts. That's why you see a range, not one number.

week5.title: Week 5: the stretch that counts
week5.body: Weeks five to eight are when most habits settle or slip. Keep the plan small enough to keep.

week6.title: Week 6: six weeks in
week6.body: Time for your first waist check, if you'd like. Next to your weight trend, it shows more of the picture.

week7.title: Week 7: you, then and now
week7.body: Week 1 next to week 7: what you logged, how steady you've been, your trend.

week8.title: Week 8: your eight weeks
week8.body: What changed, what didn't, and why. Eight weeks start a habit; the next block makes it yours.

steps_dropped.title: Your steps fell last week.
steps_dropped.body: Steps are the quiet half of what you burn: a drop can cost more than any slowdown in your metabolism. Was it a busy week?

choice.busy: Yes, life got in the way

reply.less: Aim for your step target again: a walk after training covers much of it, and it moves more than you'd think.

sessions_missed.title: A few sessions slipped by.
sessions_missed.body: It happens. What helps most is a fixed time you don't negotiate with.

reply.not_now: Fine. Your next session is on the plan as usual; nothing to make up.

loads_dropped.title: Your loads dipped a little.
loads_dropped.body: In a deficit that's normal, and it isn't muscle leaving. Keep your sets, and keep protein on target.

reply.ok: Strength comes back quickly once food goes up. Keep showing up.

hunger_first_days.title: How's your hunger so far?
hunger_first_days.body: The first days of a cut can feel easy. It's worth knowing what comes next.

reply.hungry: That's expected. It tends to settle once your meals find their rhythm.
reply.not_hungry: Enjoy it, but don't read it as a sign: hunger usually arrives around day 3 or 4, and after your first heavy leg day.

rule.first_week_on_track: When most of the week's sessions happen, the plan is working: the first week changes nothing.
rule.first_week_add_day: Four or five training days a week work best once you're past the very start; three are enough when you're new.
rule.first_week_move_missed: When sessions don't happen, days that fit your week come before a bigger plan.
rule.weight_steady_waist_down: Your weight held steady while your waist went down: the scale isn't showing everything that changed.
rule.adherence_low: When most of the plan didn't happen, the plan can't be judged yet: doing it comes before changing it.
rule.adherence_partial: Much of the plan happened, but not enough of it to tell whether the plan works.
rule.appetite_gone: A long stretch of eating more can dull your appetite; a short cut brings it back.
rule.bmr_floor: Calories never go below what your body needs at rest, so the next step comes from movement.
rule.bulk_ceiling: Past a certain point, more food in a bulk mostly adds fat, so the bulk ends there.
rule.bulk_stall: In a bulk, weight that hasn't moved toward your goal over the whole window means food goes up.
rule.bulk_step: In a bulk, calories move in small steps, so what you gain stays mostly muscle.
rule.busy_minimum_dose: In a busy week, a little training keeps what you've built: fewer sessions and sets, the same weights.
rule.calorie_change_too_soon: A new calorie target needs a couple of weeks before the scale can judge it.
rule.carb_squeeze: A lower target would crowd out the protein and carbs your training runs on, so movement goes up instead.
rule.cardio_after_lift: Cardio comes after the weights, never before, so your lifting gets your full strength.
rule.cardio_after_lift_over_line: Cardio after the weights works best kept short; a longer session is your call.
rule.cardio_build_dose: While building muscle, cardio stays light: short, easy sessions after lifting, so the food goes to your training.
rule.cardio_cut_dose: While losing fat, a short cardio session follows your training days, so the week burns a little more without taking from your lifting.
rule.cardio_off_day_low_intensity: With few training days, the extra cardio goes on a rest day at an easy pace, so the day still lets you recover.
rule.check_in_needed_adherence: Before a new plan, the coach needs to know how much of this one happened.
rule.check_in_needed_recovery: Before going further, the coach checks how you're sleeping and recovering.
rule.check_in_needed_training: Before food changes, the coach checks that your lifts are holding up.
rule.closer_to_failure: Work sets count most when they end close to failure; sets left far from it get a nudge closer.
rule.cut_step: Calories change by one clear step: big enough to show on the scale, small enough to keep up.
rule.cycle_check_needed: After a pause for low energy, one question comes before eating under your needs again.
rule.data_insufficient: A few regular weigh-ins show the trend; a single morning is mostly water.
rule.declared_context: A week you told us was disrupted isn't judged: its scale moves are mostly water and salt.
rule.double_progression: Reps climb within the range; when every set reaches the top, the weight goes up a step.
rule.energy_floor: Calories stay at the lowest level that still keeps your body fueled.
rule.fat_estimate_needed: Before calories go down, a rough read of your body shape keeps a lower target safe.
rule.fat_first: With fat to lose, losing it first makes later muscle gains show.
rule.fat_trimmed_for_carbs: Fat was trimmed toward its lower limit to leave room for the carbs your training runs on.
rule.female_fat_offset: Women's bodies naturally carry more fat, so the points for changing direction sit higher.
rule.forgiven_week_used: A single off week doesn't end your run; this was one.
rule.full_rest_week: After a run of missed sessions, a full week off lets you come back fresh.
rule.genetic_limit: Closer to your natural limit, gains come slower, so the pace eases to match.
rule.hunger_first_days: Hunger in the first days of eating less is common, and it usually settles.
rule.isolation_not_tracked: Small single-joint lifts don't judge your progress; the big lifts do.
rule.load_held_still_stalled: Holding the weight didn't move the stall, so a lighter week comes next.
rule.loads_dropped: Your weights came in under last week's, so the coach asks how things are.
rule.loads_regressed: When lifts slip, food and sleep are checked before training changes.
rule.logging_dropped: Fewer days logged than usual is often the first sign a routine is slipping.
rule.long_stagnation: Months without progress call for a lighter week to reset.
rule.loss_rate_cap: Losing faster than a steady pace costs muscle, so calories go up a step.
rule.loss_rate_cap_bodyweight: A steady pace depends on your body weight: a lighter body has a lower one.
rule.low_energy_availability: After what training burns, the plan left too little for your body to run well.
rule.low_energy_safety: A sign your body needs more fuel ends any eating under your needs.
rule.low_fat_floor: Past a certain leanness, cutting further takes more than it gives.
rule.mini_cut_over: The short cut has run its weeks; building picks up again.
rule.mini_cut_running: The short cut runs its planned weeks before anything changes.
rule.no_session_last_week: A week without a session in the first weeks is worth a word.
rule.not_toward_goal: Your weight trend isn't moving toward your goal, so the plan changes.
rule.observing: Starting calories are an estimate; the first weeks find your real maintenance.
rule.performance_red_flag: When your lifts fall, food doesn't go lower until training holds again.
rule.program_arm_weekly_sets_min: Biceps and triceps have their own weekly minimum of work sets, best split over two sessions.
rule.program_days_max: Past a handful of training days a week, the extra days cost recovery without adding growth.
rule.program_frequency: Each muscle is trained twice a week: the growth signal from one session fades after about two days.
rule.program_rep_range: Compound lifts stay in a moderate rep range and isolation moves a little higher: very low reps strain the joints, very high ones add nothing.
rule.program_weekly_sets_max: The first sets of the week do most of the growing; past a point, more sets mostly add fatigue.
rule.program_weekly_sets_min: A muscle needs a minimum of work sets each week before it has a reason to grow.
rule.plan_missed: Planned sessions fell short of the plan several weeks in a row.
rule.plan_target_needed: A change needs your current daily target to say how much.
rule.plateau: When a lift stalls, the weight holds while the reps catch up.
rule.profile_needed: Your age and height show what your body needs at rest, and a lower target stays above it.
rule.rapid_loss: A lot lost in a short time means calories go up a step.
rule.return_after_break: After a few weeks away, the first session back starts a step lighter, so the strength you kept isn't spent in a week.
rule.recovery_poor: When training holds but sleep and energy don't, recovery is what to fix.
rule.sessions_missed: Planned sessions didn't happen, so the coach asks what got in the way.
rule.stall_window: In a cut, weight that hasn't moved toward your goal over the whole window means the plan changes.
rule.steps_dropped: Your daily steps dropped, so the coach asks what changed.
rule.surplus_zone: Lean enough that cutting further costs more than it gives: building is next.
rule.technique_gate: When form wasn't clean, weight and reps hold until it is.
rule.toward_goal: Your weight is moving toward your goal, so nothing changes.
rule.training_first: Training gets sorted before any food decision.
rule.wait_one_more_week: One flat week is usually water; real change tends to show the week after.
rule.window_not_full: Your plan is judged over its full window, not before.

data_insufficient.title: Not yet. More weigh-ins first.
data_insufficient.body: One morning is mostly water. A few regular mornings show the trend, and the trend is what the call is made on.

declared_context.title: This week is paused.
declared_context.body: You told us life got in the way. A week like this moves the scale with water and salt, so nothing is read into it, and nothing is held against you. The call comes once a regular week is back.

window_not_full.title: Not yet. Your plan needs its full window.
window_not_full.body: Keep going as planned. Judging it early would read water and daily swings as progress or as a stall.

wait_one_more_week.title: Hold steady one more week.
wait_one_more_week.body: Your weight has only just paused. One flat week is usually water, and the change tends to show up all at once. Nothing changes yet.

check_in_needed_training.title: How is training going?
check_in_needed_training.body: Before any change to food, the coach needs to know whether your lifts are holding up. Log this week's sessions or answer the training question, and the call follows.

check_in_needed_recovery.title: How are you recovering?
check_in_needed_recovery.body: Your weight is moving the right way and training is holding. One question about sleep and energy decides whether anything should change.

check_in_needed_adherence.title: How much of the plan happened?
check_in_needed_adherence.body: Your weight isn't moving yet. Whether that calls for a new plan depends on how much of this one happened. Log the week and the call follows.

calorie_change_too_soon.title: Give the new target time to work.
calorie_change_too_soon.body: Your calories changed recently. A new target needs a couple of weeks before the scale can say anything about it.

observing.title: First, finding your real maintenance.
observing.body: Your starting calories are an estimate, and estimates miss by a few hundred either way. For the first weeks the plan stays put while your weigh-ins show what your body actually needs.

plan_target_needed.title: Your plan needs a calorie target first.
plan_target_needed.body: The coach can see a change is due, but it needs your current daily target to say how much. Set your plan and the call follows.

profile_needed.title: Your age and height, please.
profile_needed.body: Before lowering calories, the coach checks you won't go under what your body needs at rest. That needs your age and height.

fat_estimate_needed.title: A lower target needs one more check first.
fat_estimate_needed.body: Before calories go down, the coach needs a rough read of your body shape. That read keeps a lower target from leaving your body short of energy. Add it and the call follows; nothing else waits.

cycle_check_needed.title: One question before any cut.
cycle_check_needed.body: Your plan paused for low energy. Before you eat under your needs again, we check in once more. Your answer itself isn't saved.

increase_calories.label: Eat a little more
increase_calories.applied: Applied. Your calorie target has changed from today.

loss_rate_cap.title: Losing faster than your body can keep up.
loss_rate_cap.body: Past this pace you start losing muscle, and the extra on the scale is mostly water. Calories go up a step this week so what you lose stays fat.

rapid_loss.title: Weight came off fast. Time to ease off.
rapid_loss.body: The scale has been dropping faster than a steady pace for a while now. Calories go up a step so your body keeps up and what you lose stays fat.

low_energy_availability.title: Your plan leaves too little fuel for training.
low_energy_availability.body: After what your workouts burn, what's left is less than your body needs to run well. Calories go up so training, sleep and recovery have enough to work with.

change_movement.label: Move more
change_movement.applied: Applied. Your step goal has changed from today.

bmr_floor.title: Food stays where it is. Movement goes up.
bmr_floor.body: Another calorie cut would take you under what your body needs at rest. More daily steps keep things moving without eating less. It's a gentler push than another cut.

carb_squeeze.title: Food stays where it is. Movement goes up.
carb_squeeze.body: A lower target would leave too little room for protein and the carbs your training runs on. More daily steps keep things moving without eating less. It's a gentler push than another cut.

low_energy_safety.title: Your plan pauses here.
low_energy_safety.body: What you told us is a sign your body needs more fuel. No more eating under your needs: calories stay at least at maintenance, and it's worth talking to your doctor about it.

change_phase.label: Change direction
change_phase.applied: Applied. Your plan changes direction from today.

bulk_ceiling.title: Time to switch to a cut.
bulk_ceiling.body: Past this point, more food mostly adds fat rather than muscle. A cut now makes the next bulk count.

fat_first.title: Lose fat first.
fat_first.body: Muscle you build now would stay hidden. Most people start here, and a cut first makes every later gain visible.

surplus_zone.title: Time to switch to a bulk.
surplus_zone.body: You're lean enough that cutting further costs more than it gives. Building from here is the next step.

low_fat_floor.title: Time to stop cutting.
low_fat_floor.body: You're lean enough that eating below maintenance now takes more than it gives. Calories go up and the next phase builds.

low_energy_safety.title: Your plan pauses here.
low_energy_safety.body: What you told us is a sign your body needs more fuel. No more eating under your needs: calories stay at least at maintenance, and it's worth talking to your doctor about it.

mini_cut_over.title: The short cut is done: back to building.
mini_cut_over.body: The weeks of eating less are over. Calories go back up to where building starts, and the bulk picks up where it left off.

stop_load_increase.label: Hold the weight
stop_load_increase.applied: Applied. Your program keeps its loads from today.

plateau.title: Keep the same weight this week.
plateau.body: The lifts that stalled keep the same weight for a week before anything else changes.

deload.label: Lighter week
deload.applied: Applied. Your program is lighter this week.

load_held_still_stalled.title: A lighter week.
load_held_still_stalled.body: Holding the weight didn't move things, so this week has fewer sets. A lighter week often gives your body room to recover.

long_stagnation.title: A lighter week.
long_stagnation.body: Months at the same weights often mean tiredness has built up. This week has fewer sets; after it, build back up gradually.

full_rest_week.label: Week off
full_rest_week.applied: Applied. Your program takes the week off.

plan_missed.title: Take this week off from the gym.
plan_missed.body: For a while now the plan hasn't gone the way it was written. A lighter week rarely fixes that; a full week away does. Come back gradually after it.

loads_regressed.title: Look at food and sleep first.
loads_regressed.body: This week you couldn't lift what you lifted last week. Going backwards is rarely about the training itself: check how you ate and slept, one thing at a time.

recovery_poor.title: Your training is fine. Your recovery isn't.
recovery_poor.body: The work is getting done but you're not bouncing back. Protein and sleep come first this week; food amounts stay the same.

first_week_on_track.title: Same plan for week 2.
first_week_on_track.body: Most of your sessions happened, and that's what the first week is for. Weight and food come later, once the scale has enough mornings to say something.

first_week_too_much.title: Same plan for week 2.
first_week_too_much.body: You said week 1 felt like a lot, and every session still happened. The plan stays as it is: the same days, nothing added.

toward_goal.title: Keep going exactly as you are.
toward_goal.body: Your weight is moving the right way and nothing says it needs help. Changing a plan that works only adds noise.

energy_floor.title: Calories stay where they are.
energy_floor.body: Going lower would leave too little fuel after your training. Progress may be slower from here, and that's the safe side to be on.

mini_cut_running.title: Hold steady: the short cut runs its weeks.
mini_cut_running.body: Calories stay where the short cut set them until it ends, whatever the scale does this week. Then the bulk picks up again.

adherence_low.title: The plan comes first, not a new plan.
adherence_low.body: Less than half of the plan happened over the last few weeks. Changing calories now would change a plan that hasn't been tried. Pick the one habit that slipped most and start there.

adherence_partial.title: Close. Not enough yet to judge the plan.
adherence_partial.body: A good part of the plan happened, not quite enough to tell whether it works. Calories stay where they are while the plan gets a fair try.

performance_red_flag.title: Lifts come first. No calorie cut this week.
performance_red_flag.body: Your training is slipping while your weight isn't moving toward your goal. Cutting more now would cost muscle. Calories stay, and the focus is getting your sessions back on track.

training_first.title: Training first, food decisions later.
training_first.body: Your training is going backwards. Before anything about food changes, look at how you train: rest between sessions, sleep, and not doing too much.

adjust_calories.label: New calorie target
adjust_calories.applied: Applied. Your calorie target has changed from today.

not_toward_goal.title: Time for a new calorie target.
not_toward_goal.body: You followed the plan and your weight hasn't moved the way it should over the last few weeks. One clear step now, then a few weeks to see it work.

genetic_limit.title: Ease the pace a little.
genetic_limit.body: Your weight is moving, training and recovery are fine, but the mirror isn't keeping up. That's the pace your body can use right now, so calories move one step back toward maintenance.

mini_cut.label: Short cut
mini_cut.applied: Applied. The short cut starts today.

appetite_gone.title: A short cut to bring your appetite back.
appetite_gone.body: After a long bulk, forcing food down means the bulk has stopped paying off. A few weeks of eating less than on the bulk resets your appetite and clears some of the fat the bulk added; then the bulk picks up again.

first_week_add_day.title: Add one training day.
first_week_add_day.body: Every session happened and you said you could do more. Pick the day that suits you.
first_week_add_day.toward: One more day a week moves you toward {idealDays} days, where training works best.

first_week_move_missed.title: Same number of days, better days.
first_week_move_missed.body: Part of week 1's plan didn't happen. The number of days stays; the days themselves can move to ones that work for you. Nothing to make up.
first_week_move_missed.missed: {days} didn't happen. Pick a day that works.

logs_run_low.title: Your logs and your weight, side by side.
logs_run_low.body: Over the last few weeks your weight points to more food than your logs add up to, or to you burning more than our estimate. We can't tell those two apart, and we don't need to: your weight is what the calls are made from, so nothing here needs fixing.

logs_run_high.title: Your logs and your weight, side by side.
logs_run_high.body: Over the last few weeks your weight points to less food than your logs add up to, or to you burning less than our estimate. We can't tell those two apart, and we don't need to: your weight is what the calls are made from, so nothing here needs fixing.

health_data.title: Your health data, for your coaching
health_data.body: Your weight, waist, steps, sleep and active energy, what you conclude from your progress photos and the look you pick, your meals and recipes, your plan and check-in answers, what you tell the app about being sick, in pain or away, and the foods you avoid are health data. We use them to make your weekly calls and show your progress, and for nothing else. We never sell them or use them for ads. You can export or delete them at any time. Importing past workouts from another app also needs this consent, as they can carry your weight. You can also withdraw this consent in Settings: everything above is then deleted for good, with your past calls, except your training log, which isn't health data and stays; the calls stop until you allow it again.

apple_health.title: Connect Apple Health
apple_health.body: We read steps, sleep hours, weight from your scale, active energy and the workouts you do in other apps, so you type less and a calorie cut never goes too far. We don't read heart data, cycle data, medications, health records or location. Adding your logged workouts to Apple Health is a separate choice in Settings. You can withdraw this at any time.

third_party_ai.title: Before you analyze a meal
third_party_ai.body: Meal photos you choose to analyze, and any text you add, are sent to {provider} to estimate portions. Nothing else is sent: never your progress photos, weight, Health data, name or email. The AI explains; it doesn't decide. Weekly calls come from fixed rules you can read in every "Why this call". You can withdraw this in Settings at any time.

topic.feels_fine: Feeling good is a good sign.

permissions.healthRead: keel reads your steps, sleep, weight, active energy and workouts to make your weekly calls. It never reads heart data, cycle data, medications, health records or location.
permissions.healthWrite: keel adds to Apple Health only what you turn on in Settings: the workouts you finish, the weigh-ins you type. It writes nothing else.
permissions.camera: To read the barcode on a food pack, to take a photo of a meal you want to log, or to take your progress photos, which stay on this phone. No video or sound is recorded.
permissions.photos: To choose a photo of a meal you want to log, or a progress photo. Only the photo you pick is used.

unavailable.title: The shape projection isn't shown

unavailable.support: If eating or your body has been on your mind a lot, talking to a doctor or someone who works with eating can help.

view.title: Shape projection
view.switchNote: Off unless you turn it on.
view.offNote: A calculation from your own weigh-ins: where your weight goes in six months if you keep the plan on most days. You turn it on, and you can turn it off any time.
view.entry: Where your weight goes if you keep the plan.
view.disclaimer: This is a calculation, not a photo: the published energy balance model behind the NIH Body Weight Planner, run on your measurements and your plan. Where your body changes is individual. The model can't know it, and your result will differ.
view.options: Two ways from here: keep the plan as it is, or turn the projection off.

too_many_days.title: Train {to} days a week, not {from}
too_many_days.body: Coaching rule: {to} training days a week is the most that pays off. Your lightest day's moves go to the other days.

too_many_sets.title: {muscle}: {to} sets a week, not {from}
too_many_sets.body: Coaching rule: the first work sets do most of the growing and fatigue builds fast after them. The extra sets come off, biggest moves first.

too_few_sets.title: {muscle}: {to} sets a week, not {from}
too_few_sets.body: Coaching rule: a muscle needs at least {min} work sets a week to grow. Isolation sets top it up.

too_few_arm_sets.title: {muscle}: {to} sets a week, not {from}
too_few_arm_sets.body: Coaching rule: biceps and triceps need at least {min} work sets a week, split over two sessions. Isolation sets top it up.

once_a_week.title: {muscle} on {to} days a week
once_a_week.body: Coaching rule: train each muscle on {to} days a week. One session's growth signal fades after about two days, so part of the work moves to another day.

rep_range_compound.title: {exercise}: {toMin}-{toMax} reps
rep_range_compound.body: Coaching rule: compound lifts work best at {toMin}-{toMax} reps. Lower reps strain joints and tendons without adding growth.

rep_range_isolation.title: {exercise}: {toMin}-{toMax} reps
rep_range_isolation.body: Coaching rule: isolation moves work best at {toMin}-{toMax} reps. Going far past that adds time, not growth.
